content: I again ran into the issue that type synonyms cause defeq abuse via theorems like docs#ContinuousLinearMap.postcompUniformConvergenceCLM_apply and mainly as a metaprogramming exercise I wrote a program to find all theorems that prove an equality with the types of lhs and rhs not being reducibly equal. The output is ~15000 theorems (mainly category theory to no surprise). The question I have now is whether this is actually a problem or is that check is too strict and what is a better heuristic?
For category theory, I would say it is certainly ok if the types of the LHS and RHS match after applying dsimp (under set_option backward.defeqAttrib.useBackward true).

I would have agreed with that a while ago, but then I started trying to prove that under some conditions, the (co)Grothendieck construction is (co)complete (for the correct combination of "co"s), when I realised that it might help if we don't do this abuse... Now this might be a skill issue on my part, however I do think that the skill required can be lowered by removing this (ab)use of defeq in the category theory library.
Not using set_option backward.defeqAttrib.useBackward true would make me completely skillless. We should definitely stop abusing the phrase "defeq abuse" here.

Joël Riou said:

Not using set_option backward.defeqAttrib.useBackward true would make me completely skillless. We should definitely stop abusing the phrase "defeq abuse" here.

I absolutely agree that sometimes backward.defeqAttrib.useBackward and backward.isDefEq.transparency is unavoidable in category theory, but as a user who spends a decent amount of time into removing these kind of set_options (mostly) in RepresentationTheory, I still think we should be encouraged to create less of these when make new PRs as this would potentially cause slowdowns and make APIs very hard to use for downstream users or even other materials in mathlib. Feel free to correct me if I'm wrong!
(Also, I was specifically referring to set_option backward.defeqAttrib.useBackward true, which, with dsimp%, is my main toolbox in order to remove some set_option backward.isDefEq.transparency false)
